chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya, all from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you leave your house intending Hajj and Umrah, if God wills, recite the supplication of relief.

And it is: 'There is no god but Allah, the Forbearing, the Generous. There is no god but Allah, the Exalted, the Great. Glory be to Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the seven earths and Lord of the Great Throne.'
And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
Then say: 'O Allah, be for me a protector from every tyrant stubborn [one] and from every rebellious devil.'
Then say: 'In the name of Allah I entered, and in the name of Allah I went out, and in the path of Allah I strove.'
O Allah, I place before my forgetfulness and haste: 'In the name of Allah and what Allah willed,' during this journey of mine, whether I remembered it or forgot it.
O Allah, You are the One sought for help in all affairs, and You are the Companion in the journey and the Vicegerent in the family.
O Allah, make our journey easy for us, and contract the earth for us, and move us through it with Your obedience and the obedience of Your Messenger.
O Allah, rectify our backs (mounts), and bless us in what You have provided for us.
And protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardship of the journey, and the misery of the return, and the bad sight (of loss) regarding family, wealth, and children.
O Allah, You are my support and my helper.
O Allah, remove from me its distance and hardship, and accompany me in it, and replace me in my family with good.
And there is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Exalted, the Great.
O Allah, I am Your servant, and this is Your burden, and the Face is Your Face, and the journey is to You, and You have looked upon what no one else has looked upon.
So make this journey of mine an expiation for what preceded it of my sins, and be a help to me in it, and suffice me against its hardship and difficulty.
And teach me from speech and action that which earns Your pleasure, for I am Your servant, and by You, and for You.
So when you place your foot in the stirrup, say: 'In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate.'
In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest.
So when you are seated on your mount, and your camel is steady with you, then say:
All praise is for Allah who guided us to Islam and bestowed favor upon us.
Through Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).
Glory be to Allah.
He who has subjected to us this, and we could not have subdued it, and indeed we are to return to our Lord.
And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
O Allah, You are the One who carries on the back, and the One sought for help in the matter.
O Allah, enable us to reach a reaching that reaches to the best of reachings, reaching to Your forgiveness and pleasure.
O Allah, there is no omen except Your omen, and no good except Your good, and no guardian except You.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving home for Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a detailed ritual for departing on pilgrimage, blending general travel supplications with specific invocations for safety and sin expiation. It reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating dhikr with physical movement, transforming the journey into an act of worship that seeks divine companionship and protection from the trials of the road.
